experiment: peak working memory vs input size (constant-memory proof, Theorem 3)
instrument: tracemalloc (Python-heap allocations); the same instrument as the memory-marked test
note: The MB/s column of scale_memory is NOT a throughput measure — tracemalloc adds large timing overhead (~0.3 MB/s instrumented here). Read the peak_mb column for the memory claim, and research/results/processed/accuracy.md for throughput.
interpretation: Peak Python-heap allocation is identical (2.75 MB) as the input grows 4x (8 -> 32 MB): peak memory is independent of input size, as Theorem 3 predicts (bound ~= chunk_size + overlap + L_max).
corroboration: tests/test_memory.py::test_constant_memory_on_large_file redacts a ~1 GB generated file and asserts peak tracemalloc allocations stay below 16 MB (run with: pytest -m memory -o addopts=''). A larger scale_memory curve (e.g. --sizes 8 32 128 512) reproduces the same flat line but is slow under tracemalloc on a throttled vCPU.
